newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mixed, pork bellies higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mixed, pork bellies higher.

text.p: CME hog futures closed mixed and pork belly futures higher, with bellies supported throughout the session by bullish storage reports Tuesday, traders said.

Traders said February hogs' failure to break resistance near 76.00 cents per lb and lower live cattle futures prompted late selling in hog futures, which drove February lower and trimmed gains in other months.
However, traders remained confident hog producers should catch up on hog marketings this week after last week's harsh weather, which may allow cash prices to climb further.
Cash hogs traded mostly $0.50 per cwt higher at Midwest interior markets and $1.00 to $1.50 higher at terminal markets Wednesday.
Traders said long liquidation late trimmed gains in pork belly futures, which were sharply higher early in reaction to bullish storage reports.

USDA on Tuesday reported 38.032 million lbs of frozen pork bellies were in storage December 31, 1996, the lowest December 31 supply in 10 years. A CME report released earlier Tuesday showed 207,000 lbs of bellies were added to deliverable supplies last week, which was less than many analysts expected.
Hogs closed up 0.150 cent a lb to down 0.225 cent with February off 0.050 at 75.350 cents per lb. Pork bellies were up 0.225 to 0.800 cent with February up 0.225 at 75.525.
